artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. For finite sets $A,B$ with $|A|=|B|=N$, let $G_0\subseteq A\times B$ be a bipartite graph. We say $G_0$ is "sparsely $c(\varepsilon,\delta)$-quasirandom" (with density $p=|G_0|/N^2$) if it satisfies a standard discrepancy/codegree condition relative to the constant $p$, namely that for every $U\subseteq A$, $V\subseteq B$, $|e_{G_0}(U,V)-p|U||V||\le c(\varepsilon,\delta)\,pN^2$, together with the corresponding $C_4$-count (or two-blow-up) bound. For $G\subseteq G_0$ with $|G|\ge\delta|G_0|$, call a pair $(X,Y)\subseteq A\times B$ "$\varepsilon$-regular relative to $G_0$" if for all $X'\subseteq X$, $Y'\subseteq Y$ with $|X'|\ge\varepsilon|X|$, $|Y'|\ge\varepsilon|Y|$, one has $\bigl||G\cap(X'\times Y')|/|G_0\cap(X'\times Y')|-|G|/|G_0|\bigr|<\varepsilon$.

The following bipartite-graph statement is known: there exist functions $c(\varepsilon,\delta)$ and $C(\varepsilon,\delta)$ such that for any sparsely $c(\varepsilon,\delta)$-quasirandom $G_0$ and any $G\subseteq G_0$ with $|G|\ge\delta|G_0|$, there are equitable partitions $A=A_1\cup\cdots\cup A_s$ and $B=B_1\cup\cdots\cup B_t$ with $s,t\le C(\varepsilon,\delta)$ such that at least $(1-\varepsilon)st$ of the pairs $(i,j)$ satisfy: $G$ restricted to $A_i\times B_j$ is $\varepsilon$-regular relative to $G_0$.

Problem. Establish a $k$-uniform hypergraph analogue of this lemma. Concretely, for every $k\ge 3$, formulate and prove a regularity lemma which, given a suitably pseudorandom (in an appropriate hypergraph quasirandomness sense, e.g.\ in terms of vanishing octahedral/Gowers-type norms) sparse $k$-uniform hypergraph $H_0$ on vertex set $V$, and a subhypergraph $H\subseteq H_0$ of positive relative density, produces an equitable polyad-decomposition of $V^{(k-1)}$ of bounded complexity such that, relative to $H_0$, all but an $\varepsilon$-fraction of the polyads are $\varepsilon$-regular for $H$, with quantitative bounds independent of $|V|$.
artifact.category_tag: Hypergraph regularity in sparse pseudorandom setting
artifact.status_search_result: A relative hypergraph regularity/counting framework for subsets of sparse pseudorandom hypergraphs was developed and applied to give a new, simpler proof that the primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions. In particular, Conlon, Fox and Zhao (2013, "A relative Szemerédi theorem", arXiv:1305.5440) proved a relative Szemerédi theorem assuming only a linear-forms condition on the majorant, by means of a relative hypergraph regularity/counting approach, which yields a simplified proof of the Green–Tao theorem; related sparse hypergraph regularity/counting lemmas were also obtained by Conlon–Fox–Zhao and by Schacht/Tao and collaborators. This essentially resolves the question affirmatively.

status_evidence.title: A relative Szemerédi theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Conlon, Fox, Zhao prove a relative Szemerédi theorem under a linear-forms condition on the majorant, via a relative hypergraph regularity/counting approach, giving a simplified proof of the Green–Tao theorem.
status_evidence.claim: A hypergraph regularity-type lemma for subsets of pseudorandom sparse hypergraphs has been established and applied to give a new proof of the Green–Tao theorem.

status_evidence.title: Hypergraph regularity and the multidimensional Szemerédi theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Standard (dense) hypergraph regularity lemma developed by Gowers and by Rödl and collaborators, providing the dense base case extended in the sparse setting.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the dense hypergraph regularity framework that the relative/sparse version generalizes.
